title: Serum extracellular vesicle-associated SNORD54 adds diagnostic information to CEA and CYFRA21-1 in non-small cell lung cancer: a case-control development study.
abstract: Background Blood-based biomarkers that complement established serum markers may improve molecular classification of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We evaluated whether SNORD54 and SNORD41 measured in a serum extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and cytokeratin 19 fragment 21-1 (CYFRA21-1). Methods This single-center case-control biomarker-development study included serum samples from patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC and contemporaneous healthy controls. Supporting expression evidence was assessed in paired lung adenocarcinoma and lung squamous cell carcinoma datasets and in 48 paired formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded NSCLC specimens. Serum analyses included gene-specific cohorts and a common complete-case cohort with SNORD54, SNORD41, CEA, and CYFRA21-1 measurements. Logistic regression models were compared using paired DeLong tests. Model parsimony, adjustment for age, sex, and smoking, locked Stage I-II and Stage I subgroup analyses, U6-normalization sensitivity analyses, and 2000-resample bootstrap internal validation were performed. Results The complete-case cohort comprised 98 patients with NSCLC and 79 healthy controls. Adding SNORD54 to CEA and CYFRA21-1 increased the AUC from 0.851(95% confidence interval [CI], 0.795-0.907) to 0.951 (95% CI, 0.920-0.982; ΔAUC, 0.100; 95% CI, 0.050-0.150; P < 0.001). At the development-derived cutoff, the three-marker model achieved 85.7% sensitivity and 94.9% specificity. SNORD41 did not improve the SNORD54-containing model (ΔAUC, 0.0003; P = 0.480; likelihood-ratio P = 0.953) and increased both Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. With coefficients and the cutoff fixed from the overall cohort, the three-marker model achieved AUCs of 0.904 (95% CI, 0.843-0.964) for Stage I-II disease and 0.882 (95% CI, 0.804-0.960) for Stage I disease. SNORD54 remained informative after adjustment for age, sex, and smoking. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.948. U6 Ct values differed between diagnostic groups; associations of both snoRNAs with case status persisted in sensitivity models accounting for U6 Ct. Conclusions SNORD54 measured in a serum EV-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond CEA and CYFRA21-1 in this NSCLC case-control cohort. The parsimonious SNORD54 + CEA + CYFRA21-1 model retained discrimination in locked early-stage subgroup analyses and showed limited apparent optimism after bootstrap correction. Independent validation in cohorts that include benign pulmonary nodules and other relevant lung diseases, together with standardized EV processing and validated RNA normalization, will define the clinical transportability of this three-marker panel.

title: Characterizing age-dependent diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility properties in 5xFAD Alzheimer's mouse brain using high-resolution MRI.
abstract: Background and purpose Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating and progressive neurodegenerative disorder and the most common cause of dementia. This study aimed to characterize magnetic susceptibility changes associated with beta-amyloid (Aβ) plaques during AD progression using diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measurements in the 5xFAD mouse model. Methods Ex vivo multi-echo gradient-echo imaging (MGRE) with a spatial resolution of 40 × 40 × 40 μm 3 was performed in three age groups of 5xFAD mice (4, 12, and 18 months) using a 9.4T Bruker MRI scanner. Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) was reconstructed, and DECOMPOSE-QSM was applied to derive diamagnetic component susceptibility (DCS) and paramagnetic component susceptibility (PCS). Aβ plaques were automatically detected based on DCS and quantified to assess age-dependent plaque accumulation, changes in plaque burden, and associated susceptibility alterations. Cortical regions were further segmented into plaque-detected and plaque-undetected regions to assess regional susceptibility variations among the three age groups. In addition, Aβ/ferritin immunostaining was performed on the imaged murine brains. Results The results demonstrated progressive, spatially heterogeneous, age-dependent accumulation of amyloid plaques, as evidenced by significant increases in plaque burden. In plaque-detected and whole-region cortical areas, DCS consistently shifted toward more negative values (greater diamagnetic susceptibility) with disease progression, while PCS became more positive (greater paramagnetic susceptibility). The concurrent increase in plaque burden, together with progressively more negative DCS and more positive PCS within plaques, are consistent with increasing diamagnetic and paramagnetic tissue contributions associated with amyloid and iron-related pathology, respectively. Histological analysis showed colocalized Aβ aggregation and ferritin deposition within plaques, both of which increased with age. Conclusions The decomposed susceptibility components, DCS and PCS, provide complementary biophysical information beyond conventional QSM, enabling improved characterization of plaque-associated susceptibility changes during AD progression. High-resolution MRI facilitates the visualization and detection of individual plaques, allowing detailed analysis of their susceptibility properties. These findings highlight the importance of high-resolution MRI and the potential of diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measures as sensitive imaging biomarkers for monitoring neurodegenerative pathology.

title: Achieving detailed medial temporal lobe segmentation with upsampled isotropic training from implicit neural representation.
abstract: Imaging biomarkers in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are important tools for diagnosing, tracking and treating Alzheimer's disease (AD). Neurofibrillary tau pathology in AD is closely linked to neurodegeneration and generally follows a pattern of spread in the brain, with early stages involving subregions of the medial temporal lobe (MTL). Accurate segmentation of MTL subregions is needed to extract granular biomarkers of AD progression. MTL subregions are often imaged using T2-weighted (T2w) MRI scans that are highly anisotropic due to constraints of MRI physics and image acquisition, making it difficult to reliably model MTL subregions geometrically and extract morphological measures, such as thickness. In this study, we propose a segmentation framework for MTL subregions in isotropic space, in which an implicit neural representation is used to construct the isotropic training atlas from the anisotropic low-resolution T2w data, with T1w MRI as an auxiliary modality to support the INR and segmentation. In an independent test set, the morphological measures extracted using this isotropic model showed stronger effect sizes than those from models trained on anisotropic data in distinguishing participants with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from cognitively unimpaired individuals. In the test-retest analysis, the morphological measures extracted using the isotropic model showed greater stability than those from the anisotropic segmentation. This study demonstrates improved reliability of MRI-derived MTL subregion biomarkers without additional atlas annotation effort, which may more accurately quantify and track the relationship between AD pathology and brain atrophy for monitoring disease progression.

title: Behavioural and environmental strategies implemented by radiographers to care for patients with neurocognitive disorders during medical imaging and therapeutic procedures.
abstract: Introduction As the population ages, radiographers are increasingly likely to care for patients with dementia, Alzheimer's disease and other neurocognitive disorders in medical imaging or radiation therapy departments. Since the cognitive and behavioural presentation of these patients can vary, radiographers must be prepared to adapt their approach. To investigate behavioural and environmental strategies used by radiographers when caring for patients with neurocognitive disorders (NCDs) during medical imaging and radiation therapy procedures. Methods A cross-sectional survey comprising 18 questions was conducted among radiographers working across medical imaging and radiotherapy modalities. The questionnaire explored attitudes towards patients with NCDs, behavioural communication strategies, environmental adaptations, and institutional support measures. Descriptive statistics and thematic analysis of open-ended responses were performed. Results A total of 160 radiographers participated. Most respondents reported positive attitudes toward patients with NCDs, with 94% indicating no fear when interacting with this population. Behavioural communication strategies were frequently used, particularly maintaining eye contact (85%), using simple language (80%), and speaking slowly and clearly (76%). Caregivers were commonly involved to facilitate communication (81%). Despite this, 45% of radiographers reported frustration at not always knowing how to help effectively. Institutional environmental adaptations were limited, with most participants reporting no dementia-specific training (85%) or departmental protocols (78%). Conclusion Radiographers frequently implement behavioural strategies to support patients with NCDs, but this relies on individual initiative rather than structured organisational support, which remains limited. Implications for practice Radiographers should use clear, simple communication strategies with NCD patients, involve caregivers during imaging procedures, and develop dementia-specific training and departmental protocols.

title: MRI-Only Preoperative Localization and Semiautomated Three-Dimensional Modeling of the Cervical Vagus Nerve for Vagus Nerve Stimulation Implantation.
abstract: Background We evaluated whether three-dimensional steady-state free precession with time-spatial labeling inversion pulse (3D-SSFP with time-SLIP) MRI could localize the cervical vagus nerve before vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) implantation and developed training-data-free semiautomated vagus nerve tracking software. Methods Thirty patients with drug-resistant epilepsy underwent preoperative cervical 3D-SSFP with time-SLIP MRI followed by VNS implantation. The left vagus nerve was visually identified at the planned surgical level, and its relationship to the common carotid artery (CCA) and internal jugular vein (IJV) was classified. MRI localization was validated against intraoperative findings. A MATLAB-based tool semi-automatically tracked the vagus nerve, CCA, and IJV from user-defined reference points. Accuracy was assessed using coordinate error and classification agreement. Results The vagus nerve was identified on MRI in all 30 patients, with complete concordance between MRI and intraoperative localization. Among 29 classifiable patients, the nerve was located superficially between the CCA and IJV in 45%, superficially and lateral to the CCA in 41%, deep between the CCA and IJV in 10%, and deep and medial to the CCA in 3.4%. The median distance between software-derived and visually identified coordinates was 1 mm (interquartile range, 1-2 mm), and software-derived classification agreed with consensus visual classification in 27 of 29 patients (93%). Conclusions Cervical MRI enabled preoperative localization of the vagus nerve and adjacent vessels. The semiautomated method showed close agreement with expert visual assessment and may support anatomical orientation and surgical planning for VNS implantation.

title: Retrieval-induced forgetting and facilitation across the Alzheimer's disease continuum: Behavioral and neuroanatomical evidence from a recognition-based paradigm.
abstract: Objective The aim of the present study was to investigate facilitation (FAC) and retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF) during episodic memory retrieval across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum and to examine their gray matter correlates in verbal and visual recognition tasks. Method One hundred participants (28 AD, 29 amnestic mild cognitive impairment, 23 subjective cognitive decline [SCD], 20 healthy subjects) completed a modified retrieval-practice paradigm (mRPP) involving verbal and visual recognition tasks, a comprehensive neuropsychological battery, and 3T magnetic resonance imaging. FAC and RIF were computed at the group level and via individual proxy scores, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess the association between mRPP indices and regional gray matter volumes. Results The verbal mRPP showed reduced overall recognition in AD compared with healthy subjects ( p = .003 - η p ² = 0.23). A robust FAC effect in AD, amnestic mild cognitive impairment, and SCD was observed, whereas RIF emerged only in SCD, suggesting intact inhibitory control at the earliest stage and its disruption with disease progression ( p < .001 - η p ² = 0.48). The visual mRPP showed a strong FAC effect across all groups, with no RIF, indicating modality-specific reliance on recognition-based retrieval ( p < .001 - η p ² = 0.63). Voxel-based morphometry analyses revealed distinct gray matter correlates across groups and tasks: Verbal RIF was negatively associated with frontotemporal regions in AD patients and parieto-occipital regions in healthy subjects, while visual indices showed widespread associations with temporal, subcortical, cerebellar, and sensorimotor regions, particularly in amnestic mild cognitive impairment and SCD groups. Conclusions This study shows shared and modality-specific brain mechanisms of retrieval practice across AD stages. Preserved compensatory processes in SCD individuals give way to progressive regional disruption, supporting early, modality-tailored, and multimodal cognitive interventions to enhance cognition and delay cognitive decline. title: Cardiometabolic health's influence on the efficacy of pre-operative hormone therapy for men with localized high-risk prostate cancer.
abstract: Background Altered lipid metabolism, adiposity, and androgens have been linked to cardiac disease and prostate cancer. Adiposity increases risk of recurrence for prostate cancer and may enhance response to androgen receptor pathway inhibition (ARPI). We evaluated whether adiposity and circulating lipid metabolites are associated with response to pre-operative ADT + /- ARPI in localized high-risk prostate cancer (HRPCa). Methods We performed a post hoc analysis of 104 men with localized HRPCa treated with 3-6 months of preoperative ADT + /- ARPI across three trials. Body composition was quantified from L3 CT imaging at baseline and at radical prostatectomy (RP; end-of-treatment [EOT] n = 56). Plasma lipid metabolites were profiled by UPLC-MS at baseline (n = 60) and in paired baseline/EOT samples (n = 59). Pathologic response was defined as ≤ T2N0 at RP. PSA progression-free survival (PFS) was defined as time from RP to PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL or initiation of radiotherapy. Results Median age was 63 years, 76.9% had Gleason grade group 4-5, and 43.7% had clinical T3-4 disease. At RP, lower visceral (VATi, p = 0.002) and subcutaneous adiposity (SATi, p = 0.004) were associated with pathologic response. Increasing adiposity at RP was associated with PSA progression (per 10-unit increase: VATi HR 1.09, p = 0.04; SATi HR 1.14, p = 0.03). In paired analyses (n = 59), pathologic responders demonstrated decreases (p < 0.05) in diacylglycerols and polyunsaturated fatty acyl chain-containing triacylglycerols (PUFA-TAGs) and elevations in ceramide species. Non-responders exhibited increases (p < 0.05) in PUFA-TAGs and glycerophospholipids with reductions in lysophosphatidylcholine species, long-chain acylcarnitine, and cholesterol. Conclusions Higher post-treatment adiposity and intrapatient changes in lipid metabolite pathways were associated with inferior outcomes after pre-operative hormone therapy, supporting a stage-dependent link between cardiometabolic health and prostate cancer that warrants further elucidation.

title: Current classification systems in slipped capital femoral epiphysis: Clinical relevance, limitations, and future directions.
abstract: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) is the most common adolescent hip disorder and remains a significant cause of pain, gait disturbance, proximal femoral deformity, and early degenerative hip disease. Accurate classification of SCFE is essential for diagnosis, prognostication, treatment planning, and communication among orthopedic surgeons. Over the past several decades, multiple classification systems have been proposed based on symptom duration, physeal stability, radiographic severity, and deformity morphology. However, substantial variability exists regarding their reliability, prognostic value, and clinical applicability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the currently available classification systems in SCFE, including temporal, Loder, Southwick, Wilson, epiphyseal tubercle (Maranho), MRI-based, and three-dimensional/statistical shape modeling classifications. Particular emphasis is placed on their historical evolution, clinical relevance, prognostic implications, limitations, and emerging role in modern hip preservation strategies. Among existing systems, the Loder classification remains the most clinically influential because of its strong association with avascular necrosis risk, while the Southwick classification continues to play a central role in quantifying deformity severity and guiding surgical decision-making. Emerging imaging-based and three-dimensional classifications have improved understanding of the rotational and multiplanar nature of SCFE and may facilitate earlier diagnosis, improved deformity characterization, and individualized treatment planning. Nevertheless, no single classification system comprehensively integrates physeal stability, deformity severity, vascular compromise, cartilage injury, and long-term functional prognosis. Current SCFE classification systems remain valuable tools in contemporary clinical practice; however, important limitations persist regarding reproducibility, prognostic accuracy, and integration with modern biomechanical concepts. Future classification frameworks may benefit from a multidomain approach integrating physeal stability, deformity morphology, vascular and biological status, cartilage involvement, and patient-specific prognostic factors, with prospective multicentre validation required before clinical adoption.

Future classification frameworks may benefit from a multidomain approach integrating physeal stability, deformity morphology, vascular and biological status, cartilage involvement, and patient-specific prognostic factors, with prospective multicentre validation required before clinical adoption.

title: Acute Enlargement of a Frontal Calvarial Lesion in Polyostotic Fibrous Dysplasia Associated with McCune-Albright Syndrome: A Case Report.
abstract: Background McCune-Albright syndrome is a rare mosaic disorder caused by postzygotic activating mutations in GNAS , classically presenting with fibrous dysplasia (FD), hyperpigmented macules, and endocrinopathies. Craniofacial FD is common and typically follows a benign course. However, acute symptomatic changes with aggressive imaging features may mimic malignant transformation or secondary lesions such as aneurysmal bone cysts (ABCs), creating significant diagnostic uncertainty. Case Description We report a 20-year-old woman with known MAS and polyostotic FD who presented with a 4-week history of progressive left frontal swelling, headache, and tenderness. Interval imaging revealed a rapidly enlarging erosive lytic lesion of the left frontal calvarium with peripheral enhancement and an internal fluid-fluid level, raising concern for secondary pathology or malignancy. Given rapid growth and cortical erosion, the patient underwent surgical resection with cranioplasty. Intraoperatively, the lesion contained serosanguinous fluid. Histopathology demonstrated bland spindle cell proliferation with curvilinear woven bone trabeculae and hemosiderin-laden macrophages, without cytologic atypia, necrosis, or features of ABC. Molecular testing confirmed a GNAS p.(R201C) mutation, consistent with FD. The patient had an uncomplicated postoperative course with complete symptom resolution. Conclusion This case highlights that fluid-fluid levels, rapid interval growth, and erosive changes can occur in craniofacial FD without ABC formation or malignant transformation. Imaging findings alone are insufficient to distinguish benign changes from aggressive pathology. Accurate diagnosis requires a multimodal approach integrating clinical context, advanced imaging, histopathology, and pathologic analysis. Surgical intervention is justified in some cases to establish diagnosis and provide symptomatic relief.

title: Tenosynovitis caused by Mycobacterium malmoense.
abstract: Background Mycobacterium malmoense is a slow-growing nontuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) increasingly recognized as a cause of extrapulmonary infections. Tenosynovitis due to M. malmoense is rare and diagnostically challenging because of its indolent course and nonspecific clinical presentation. Case presentation We report a 65-year-old immunocompetent woman presenting with progressive wrist pain, swelling, and impaired hand function without prior trauma. Symptoms developed after exposure to fresh fish and shellfish. Surgical exploration revealed extensive tenosynovitis with median nerve compression. Histopathology showed granulomatous synovitis suggestive of mycobacterial infection. Molecular testing detected Mycobacterium genus DNA, while PCR for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex was negative. After prolonged incubation, culture identified M. malmoense . Drug susceptibility testing demonstrated susceptibility to standard antimycobacterial agents except doxycycline. Initial empiric therapy targeting M. marinum was adapted following species identification. After 8 months of treatment, significant clinical and radiological improvement was observed, with no evidence of relapse at 6-month follow-up. Discussion M. malmoense tenosynovitis is extremely rare, with only few cases reported. Diagnosis is frequently delayed due to low sensitivity of microscopy, slow growth in culture, and nonspecific findings. Molecular diagnostics and prolonged incubation are essential. Management requires a combination of surgery and prolonged antimycobacterial therapy. Conclusion NTM infections, including M. malmoense , should be considered in chronic tenosynovitis unresponsive to standard treatment. Early diagnostic suspicion and interdisciplinary management are crucial for favorable outcomes.

title: Multimodal based Brain Tumor Classification using Clustered Federated Learning in Edge based IoT Network.
abstract: A brain tumor is characterized by the uncontrolled growth of cells that causes a severe impact on the quality of life. Nowadays, various methods based on multimodal medical images are used to identify brain tumors. Meanwhile, these methods require extensive amounts of labeled information to identify disease tissues and often encounter various challenges based on privacy and accuracy. This paper establishes a Taylor-based Focal Log-cosh Entropy Network (TFLE-Net) to classify brain tumors from demographic data and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images by utilizing clustered federated learning in an edge-based Internet of Things (IoT) network. The detection process is executed in clustered federated learning concerning two entities: server and nodes. In a local training model, an input MRI scan is pre-processed, further brain tumor areas are segmented, and then, the mining of various features is performed. Simultaneously, the normalization of input demographic data is done, and the suitable features are selected using information gain. Further, the extracted features and chosen features are subjected to TFLE-Net to classify brain tumors. Additionally, the TFLE-Net yielded Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.057, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.047, True Positive Rate (TPR) of 97.789%, and accuracy of 96.987%.

title: Posterior Scleritis Following Uneventful Small-Incision Cataract Surgery.
abstract: Background Posterior scleritis following routine, uncomplicated cataract surgery in a patient without underlying systemic disease is an exceedingly rare and potentially sight-threatening clinical entity. Method A 55-year-old female with no systemic medical history presented three weeks after uneventful small-incision cataract surgery (SICS) in the right eye with sudden vision loss, redness, and severe ocular pain exacerbated by eye movements. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) had deteriorated from 6/9 to finger counting close to her face. Dilated fundus examination revealed multiple dull yellow subretinal lesions across the posterior pole. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed hyperreflective vitreous cells, subretinal fluid (SRF), and choroidal undulations. B-scan ultrasonography confirmed diffuse posterior scleritis, demonstrating localized sclerochoroidal thickening and fluid accumulation in the sub-Tenon's space. Comprehensive laboratory testing and imaging ruled out infectious and autoimmune etiologies. Result The patient was treated with high-dose intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (1 g/day for three days) followed by an oral prednisolone taper, which led to immediate pain relief and anatomical resolution. At six months, the scleritis had completely resolved with a BCVA improvement to 6/12, limited by persistent localized disruption of the foveal ellipsoid zone on OCT. The patient remained recurrence-free at six months. Conclusion Diffuse posterior scleritis can occur as a postoperative inflammatory phenomenon following uneventful cataract surgery. Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion, utilize B-scan ultrasonography for diagnosis, and initiate prompt systemic corticosteroid therapy to optimize anatomical and visual outcomes.

title: Bone microarchitecture, density, and strength assessment in automotive trauma patients using HR-pQCT: a pilot study.
abstract: Objective Automotive trauma patients enrolled in the Crash Injury Research and Engineering Network (CIREN) typically undergo computed tomography (CT) imaging as part of emergency care. HR-pQCT is a noninvasive imaging technique that enables assessment of bone microarchitecture at the peripheral sites. CT and HR-pQCT can be used to estimate volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) and strength via finite element analysis (FEA). However, HR-pQCT's superior resolution (approximately 10 times higher than conventional clinical CT scanners) captures in vivo trabecular and cortical microarchitecture, enabling high fidelity FEA. This study examines HR-pQCT-derived bone microarchitecture and strength measurements in relation to fracture patterns, bone-related comorbidities, and CT-derived vBMD in CIREN trauma patients, while providing foundational evidence to support HR-pQCT use following motor vehicle crashes (MVC) and pedestrian crashes. Methods Nine automotive trauma patients (ages 17-76; 78% female) enrolled at Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center from the National Highway Safety Administration's CIREN study participated in the HR-pQCT pilot study. HR-pQCT scans were acquired within 1-12 months following the patient's MVC ( n = 7) or pedestrian crash ( n = 2). Scans were acquired at four sites: 1) distal tibia, 2) diaphyseal tibia, 3) distal radius, and 4) diaphyseal radius. HR-pQCT normative percentiles were determined using Indiana University's calculator. Descriptive statistics were used to present HR-pQCT musculoskeletal outcomes based on bone-related comorbidities, BMI, and fracture incidence. Pearson correlations were performed between HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia and radius total vBMD and CT-derived total vBMD at the spine and femoral compartments. Results At the distal tibia, participants without tibia and fibula fractures tended to show greater mean cortical thickness (1.63 ± 0.38 versus 1.15 ± 0.05 mm), cortical area (146.24 ± 46.07 versus 103.70 ± 1.70 mm 2 ), cortical vBMD (943.83 ± 79.18 versus 861.05 ± 26.52 mg HA/cm 3 ), and bone strength (10.25 ± 3.72 versus 7.00 ± 0.70 kN). Additionally, HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia total vBMD demonstrated a strong positive correlation with CT-derived femoral head total vBMD ( r = 0.766; p = 0.045). Normative percentiles showed that participants with bone-related comorbidities had lower bone microarchitectural and strength percentiles than the group without comorbidities. Conclusion This study demonstrates the viability of HR-pQCT for characterizing bone microarchitecture, strength, and density in automotive trauma patients and identifying differences that might relate to fracture and bone-related comorbidities. These preliminary findings support incorporating HR-pQCT imaging into automotive crash research due to its ability to provide detailed cortical and trabecular microarchitectural measurements that are not available from clinical CT.

title: Spinal neurocysticercosis: synthesizing evidence on clinical presentations, anatomical patterns, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Spinal neurocysticercosis (NCC) is an uncommon manifestation of NCC involving the spinal cord, meninges, nerve roots, and subarachnoid spaces. Although less common than intracranial disease, spinal involvement can cause substantial neurological morbidity because even small lesions within the confined spinal canal may produce progressive myelopathy. Disease may result from hematogenous dissemination or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) spread of Taenia solium larvae and may present as intramedullary, intradural extramedullary, subarachnoid, or, rarely, extradural lesions. Clinical manifestations are diverse and include paraparesis, quadriparesis, cauda equina syndrome, and chronic meningitis. Magnetic resonance imaging is the diagnostic modality of choice, providing detailed assessment of lesion location, evolutionary stage, inflammatory activity, and associated complications. CSF analysis and immunological or molecular tests provide supportive evidence, while histopathological examination confirms the diagnosis when tissue is available. Treatment is individualized and may include antiparasitic agents, corticosteroids, and surgery when indicated. Although outcomes are generally favorable with early diagnosis and appropriate treatment, delayed treatment, extensive arachnoiditis, diffuse leptomeningeal disease, and established spinal cord damage may result in permanent neurological deficits. Further prospective studies are needed to refine diagnostic strategies and optimize management. PubMed database was searched from inception to 13 July 2026, for spinal neurocysticercosis and spinal cysticercosis.

title: GPT-assisted radiomic modeling for predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Objective . To evaluate whether GPT can assist in automating radiomics modeling for predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Methods. The study included a training cohort (TC; n = 186), a validation cohort (VC; n = 116), and a prospective multicenter validation cohort (PVC; n = 269). Radiomic and supervised deep learning features were extracted from pretreatment T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging. logistic regression (LR) was first evaluated using radiomic, deep learning, and fused features. Support vector machine, naïve Bayes, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting models were subsequently compared using fused features. GPT was not used as the classifier but assisted with preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, code generation and execution, model training, and probability output. Each GPT-assisted workflow was independently repeated five times. Results. Fused features achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for both manually developed and GPT-assisted LR models. Their AUCs were 0.759 versus 0.763 ± 0.003 in the TC, 0.714 versus 0.741 ± 0.008 in the VC, and 0.700 versus 0.706 ± 0.004 in the PVC. Across five classifiers, GPT-assisted workflows achieved performance broadly comparable to manually developed models. Repeated GPT-assisted runs showed limited variability, with AUC standard deviations ranging from 0.001 to 0.019. Conclusion. Under expert supervision, GPT can automate key radiomics modeling procedures while achieving performance comparable to conventional machine learning workflows, potentially reducing technical workload and facilitating integrated model development.

title: Multi-GPU parallel framework for DOI-enabled long axial field-of-view PET image reconstruction.
abstract: Objective. Depth-of-interaction (DOI)-enabled long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) positron emission tomography (PET) can mitigate parallax-induced resolution degradation, but DOI modeling substantially expands the lines-of-response space and increases computational cost. This study aimed to develop a scalable reconstruction framework for DOI-enabled LAFOV-PET. Approach. We present an optimized multi-GPU reconstruction framework based on list-mode ordered-subsets expectation maximization. The framework targets the major computational bottlenecks of DOI-enabled LAFOV-PET reconstruction, including sensitivity image calculation and Monte Carlo-based scatter estimation. Main results. The extended IQ phantom demonstrated near-linear scalability across multiple GPUs for sensitivity image calculation and Monte Carlo-based scatter estimation. Additional Derenzo and hybrid anthropomorphic phantom studies validated the imaging benefits of DOI modeling, including improved spatial resolution and performance under realistic imaging conditions. Significance. The proposed framework improves the scalability of DOI-enabled LAFOV-PET reconstruction by enabling its dominant computational components to efficiently utilize available GPU resources, establishing a foundation for high-performance reconstruction in next-generation PET systems.

title: X-ray projection-guided deformation vector field estimation and dynamic CBCT imaging using patient-specific vector-quantized diffusion.
abstract: Objective. To develop a conditional vector-quantized (VQ) diffusion-based dynamic cone beam computed tomography imaging framework using dual-view x-ray projections for accurate reconstruction of respiratory-induced lung tumor motion, with the potential to enable four-dimensional (4D) target verification during lung radiotherapy. Methods. Patient-specific respiratory motion models were constructed from planning 4D- computed tomography(CT) images using deformable image registration and principal component analysis (PCA). Synthetic DVFs were generated by sampling PCA coefficients and applied to the reference-phase CT images to produce dynamic three-dimensional (3D) volumes, from which paired dual-view DRRs were generated. A conditional VQ diffusion framework was developed, consisting of separate two-dimensional and 3D vector quantized variational autoencoder s for encoding DRRs and DVFs into discrete latent representations, followed by a conditional diffusion model to learn the mapping from x-ray projection features to deformation vector field (DVF) latent representations. During inference, dual-view x-ray projections were encoded and processed by the conditional diffusion model to estimate DVFs, which were then used to deform the reference CT image and reconstruct temporally resolved 3D volumes. Results. The simulation study demonstrates that the estimated DVFs effectively captured the respiratory-induced deformation of lung tumors, and the reconstructed dynamic volume CT images demonstrated accurate anatomical motion characteristics across respiratory phases. Conclusion. The proposed patient-specific VQ diffusion framework enables accurate estimation of respiratory-induced lung tumor motion from dual-view x-ray projections and facilitates the high-temporal-resolution dynamic volume CT reconstruction. The results demonstrate its potential as an image-guided solution for tumor motion tracking in lung tumor radiotherapy.

title: Real-time assessment of mitotic rate in malignant melanoma by ex vivo confocal microscopy.
abstract: Background Malignant melanoma has exhibited a significant increase in incidence over the past decade and remains the most common cause of skin cancer-related deaths. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential, as delays correlate with poorer clinical outcomes. Ex vivo confocal laser scanning microscopy (EVCM) enables intraoperative examination of fresh tissues within minutes and has shown potential for detecting morphological criteria and accurately determining Breslow thickness in melanoma. Objectives The aim of the present pilot study was to evaluate whether EVCM can also reliably assess the mitotic rate, an important prognostic marker influencing the indication for sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB). Methods 40 histologically confirmed melanomas from various anatomical sites were examined using the current gold standard of histopathology and EVCM. The confocal mitotic rate (CMR) and the histopathological mitotic rate (HMR) were statistically compared. In this context, two clinically relevant groups (0 mitoses/mm2 and ≥ 1 mitosis/mm2) were defined for analysis, taking into consideration the clinically significant thresholds typically used in histopathological assessment. Results Overall, 95.0% of melanomas were correctly assigned to the respective group. With a sensitivity of 100%, a specificity of 77.8%, a positive predictive value of 93.9% and a negative predictive value of 100%, EVCM demonstrated promising performance for detecting mitotic activity. Conclusions These findings emphasize the potential of EVCM for reliable detection of atypical mitotic figures. Prior to clinical implementation, prospective validation in larger, multicenter cohorts involving multiple EVCM experts is required.

title: Association between Glycoprotein Acetylation-Indicated Inflammation and Small HDL Particle Number in Coronary Artery Disease.
abstract: Background Glycoprotein acetylation (GlycA) is a nuclear magnetic resonance-derived biomarker of systemic inflammation. GlycA shows statistical interaction with small HDL particle number (s-HDL-P) in relation to coronary artery disease (CAD). This study examines the confounding effects of GlycA-related glycoproteins, hypertriglyceridemia, and s-HDL-P on CAD risk. Methods Plasma samples from 752 participants in the CATHGEN biorepository were size-fractionated by asymmetric flow field-flow fractionation and analyzed by targeted proteomics and lipidomics. Fraction concentrations were converted to HDL particle number using a volumetric approach based on apolipoprotein A-I (APOA1) concentration, HDL size, and lipoprotein lipid composition. Correlations between GlycA, glycoproteins, total triglyceride (TG), HDL composition and HDL particle number, and their associations with CAD were assessed using multivariate least-squares fit and nominal logistic regression analysis, respectively. Results Acute-phase inflammation-related glycoproteins (GlycA-proteins) correlated strongly with GlycA. However, the size-distribution profiles of GlycA-proteins were consistent with circulation as free dimers/trimers, and their lack of overlap with APOA1 profiles suggested no detectable HDL binding. In contrast, apolipoproteins and lipid transfer proteins showed size-profile shifts relative to APOA1 consistent with HDL binding. s-HDL-P showed an inverse association with GlycA, most significantly at low TG levels. In CAD models, significant GlycA × s-HDL-P interaction emerged only when TG was included as a covariate. CAD correlated with lipoprotein lipids, apolipoproteins, and lipid transfer proteins that influence lipoprotein remodeling. Conclusions GlycA-proteins circulate freely without direct HDL binding. The empirical GlycA × s-HDL-P interaction is consistent with indirect coupling between systemic inflammation and altered lipoprotein remodeling associated with CAD risk.

title: When to stop monitoring pituitary stalk thickening?
abstract: Pituitary stalk thickening (PST) in adults may arise from neoplastic, inflammatory, infectious, or congenital disease, yet the underlying cause frequently remains undetermined after initial evaluation. For patients without an established diagnosis, no adult-specific data defines how long magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) surveillance should be maintained. Current expert reviews recommend early reassessment at 3-6 months, followed by longitudinal imaging for approximately 3-5 years. Among initially indeterminate lesions, spontaneous regression is more likely than the progression, although late diagnosis of histiocytic disease can nevertheless occur. We suggest reducing MRI frequency after sustained stability and considering discontinuation only in carefully selected low-risk adults, while maintaining longer surveillance whenever endocrine, radiological, or systemic risk features persist.

title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Tumor-Derived DNA Analysis Aids in the Diagnosis of Postpartum Diffuse Midline Glioma.
abstract: Background Gliomas diagnosed during pregnancy or postpartum pose diagnostic and management challenges. Neurologic symptoms may be attributed to physiological changes of pregnancy or the postpartum state, possibly delaying evaluation. When lesions arise in high-risk locations, such as the brainstem, tissue biopsy is frequently infeasible, further complicating the diagnostic process. Patient presentation A 28-year-old woman developed dysphagia during pregnancy, which persisted and gradually worsened after delivery. Postpartum evaluation identified a right thyroid nodule, subsequently diagnosed as papillary thyroid carcinoma following hemithyroidectomy. Eight months postpartum, the patient experienced progressive dysphagia, headaches, and dizziness. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an expansile medullary lesion concerning for a high-grade primary brainstem tumor. Due to the brainstem location, biopsy was infeasible, and empiric chemoradiation was initiated for presumed high-grade glioma. Molecular findings Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tumor-derived nucleic acid analysis using Summit™ 2.0 identified an H3-3A K28M alteration, along with co-occurring pathogenic alterations in NF1 and TP53. In conjunction with the clinical and radiographic findings, these molecular results supported classification of the tumor as diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered. Management and outcome Following completion of chemoradiation, dordaviprone therapy was initiated. At the most recent documented follow-up in January 2026, brain MRI demonstrated decreased size and enhancement of the medullary lesion, accompanied by improvement in dysphagia, headaches, dystonic movements, balance, and overall performance status. Conclusions This case demonstrates that cerebrospinal fluid-based genomic profiling can provide clinically meaningful molecular information when tissue diagnosis is contraindicated and can inform treatment planning for patients with anatomically inaccessible central nervous system tumors. It also highlights the significance of ongoing evaluation of persistent neurologic symptoms during pregnancy and the postpartum period.

Gliomas diagnosed during pregnancy or postpartum pose diagnostic and management challenges. Neurologic symptoms may be attributed to physiological changes of pregnancy or the postpartum state, possibly delaying evaluation. When lesions arise in high-risk locations, such as the brainstem, tissue biopsy is frequently infeasible, further complicating the diagnostic process.

Patient presentation

A 28-year-old woman developed dysphagia during pregnancy, which persisted and gradually worsened after delivery. Postpartum evaluation identified a right thyroid nodule, subsequently diagnosed as papillary thyroid carcinoma following hemithyroidectomy. Eight months postpartum, the patient experienced progressive dysphagia, headaches, and dizziness. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an expansile medullary lesion concerning for a high-grade primary brainstem tumor. Due to the brainstem location, biopsy was infeasible, and empiric chemoradiation was initiated for presumed high-grade glioma.

Molecular findings

Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tumor-derived nucleic acid analysis using Summit™ 2.0 identified an H3-3A K28M alteration, along with co-occurring pathogenic alterations in NF1 and TP53. In conjunction with the clinical and radiographic findings, these molecular results supported classification of the tumor as diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered.

Management and outcome

Following completion of chemoradiation, dordaviprone therapy was initiated. At the most recent documented follow-up in January 2026, brain MRI demonstrated decreased size and enhancement of the medullary lesion, accompanied by improvement in dysphagia, headaches, dystonic movements, balance, and overall performance status.

Conclusions

This case demonstrates that cerebrospinal fluid-based genomic profiling can provide clinically meaningful molecular information when tissue diagnosis is contraindicated and can inform treatment planning for patients with anatomically inaccessible central nervous system tumors. It also highlights the significance of ongoing evaluation of persistent neurologic symptoms during pregnancy and the postpartum period.

title: Feasibility of opportunistic osteoporosis screening using ankle CT Hounsfield units in older adults with ankle fractures.
abstract: Background Fragility fractures reveal osteoporosis, but ankle fractures are not consistently defined as fragility fractures. CT-derived Hounsfield unit measurements may provide an opportunistic method to identify patients at risk for osteoporosis. Purpose This study investigated the relationship between Hounsfield units (HU) from ankle CT scans and bone mineral density (BMD) measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), with the aim of determining whether sufficient signal exists between ankle HU and DEXA-derived BMD to justify a larger prospective validation study, rather than to establish a definitive diagnostic tool. Study design/level of evidence Retrospective correlation study. Level III. Methods Patients aged 55 years or older, who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for OTA/AO 44 A-C ankle fractures between 2012 and 2024 and had both a preoperative ankle CT and a DEXA scan within 1 year of injury, were reviewed. HU values of the distal tibia and fibula were measured using standardized elliptical regions of interest. Multivariate linear regression was performed with the lowest DEXA T-score as the dependent variable, with HU values, and BMI as independent variables. Results A total of 57 patients (87.7% female, mean age 69.67 ± 9.24 years) were included. The average ankle HU was 192.43 ± 60.04, and the mean T-score was -1.73 ± 0.96. Regression analysis demonstrated that HU values (B = 0.005, P = .021) and BMI (B = 0.064, P = .007) were positively correlated with the T-score.The regression model was lowest T-score = 0.005*Ankle HU + 0.064*BMI-4.422.Based on this equation, an HU measurement of 106.64 or less, assuming a BMI of 21.7, correlated with osteoporosis. Conclusions Ankle HU values from CT scans demonstrated a positive association with DEXA-derived BMD, supporting proof-of-concept for ankle HU as a preliminary screening tool and providing methodological groundwork for future prospective validation. Given the high prevalence of osteopenia or osteoporosis in this population, ankle fractures should prompt formal bone health evaluation.

title: Neutrophilic Fixed Drug Eruption Mimicking Neutrophilic Dermatosis: Two Cases, Including Sequential Biopsies Demonstrating Time-Dependent Histopathology.
abstract: Abstract Fixed drug eruption (FDE) is classically a lymphocyte-predominant interface dermatitis, but an early lesion may show a prominent neutrophilic infiltrate that closely simulates a primary neutrophilic dermatosis. We report 2 cases. The first, a 42-year-old woman, developed a multifocal eruption approximately 45 minutes after re-exposure to etoricoxib, recurring at previously affected and new sites. A punch biopsy performed 21 hours after ingestion of the drug showed a basketweave stratum corneum, intense papillary dermal edema with pseudovesiculation, and a superficial and deep infiltrate rich in neutrophils with karyorrhexis, closely resembling Sweet syndrome. Only occasional apoptotic keratinocytes were present within the epidermis, and the marked edema obscured any interface dermatitis, although admixed eosinophils were noted. Clinicopathologic correlation ultimately established the diagnosis of neutrophilic FDE. The second, a 55-year-old man, had an eruption recurring at the same sites after pseudoephedrine. A biopsy of an established lesion 2-3 weeks after ingestion showed classic interface dermatitis with numerous eosinophils and pigment incontinence, whereas one taken from the same region within 24 hours of re-exposure showed a neutrophil-predominant infiltrate with prominent karyorrhexis and only focal interface change. These cases, biopsied at documented time points, support the concept that the neutrophil-rich appearance of FDE represents an early phase in its histopathologic evolution, demonstrate how it can be mistaken for a neutrophilic dermatosis in the absence of adequate clinical history, and show that clinicopathologic correlation and a high index of suspicion are necessary to reliably arrive at the correct diagnosis.

title: Congenital Melanocytic Nevus Mimicking a Coccygeal Pad in the Sacrococcygeal Region.
abstract: Congenital melanocytic nevus (CMN) is a benign melanocytic proliferative lesion that presents at birth or in early infancy. When the lesion extends into the deep dermis or subcutaneous tissue, it can form a mass that is clinically and radiologically indistinguishable from other soft tissue tumors. We report a case of sacrococcygeal CMN mimicking a coccygeal pad. An 18-year-old man presented with a sacrococcygeal mass and tenderness. Magnetic resonance imaging and needle biopsy findings suggested a coccygeal pad. Because of persistent pain and the patient's desire for removal, the mass was excised under general anesthesia with periosteal inclusion, and the resulting 95 × 50 mm defect was reconstructed using a right superior gluteal artery perforator flap. Histopathological examination confirmed CMN without malignant features. The flap survived completely, and the postoperative course was uneventful. Tenderness resolved completely, and no local or symptomatic recurrence was observed at 6 months. CMN should be considered in the differential diagnosis of sacrococcygeal masses, and needle biopsy may be insufficient for diagnosing deeply infiltrating lesions.

title: Multicompartmental hemorrhage: A high-risk pattern associated with increased risk for progression in TBI patients.
abstract: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) with intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) often requires repeat head computed tomography (CT) imaging to monitor for bleed progression. While prior literature has explored patient-level factors, data on the impact of ICH morphologies (subdural [SDH], epidural [EDH], intraparenchymal [IPH], intraventricular [IVH], and multicompartment hemorrhage [MCH]) on radiographic ICH progression remains unclear. We hypothesized that MCH and IVH would have an increased associated risk of progression. Methods This retrospective (2021-2023) single-center cohort included adults (≥18 y) with TBI-related ICH who underwent initial and repeat head CT. Patients were stratified into radiographic progression versus no-progression cohorts, with progression defined as new or enlarging hemorrhage on attending radiologist interpretation of follow-up head CT. The primary outcome was the rate of radiographic progression for each ICH type. MCH was defined as the presence of two or more ICH types. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the association between each ICH type and radiographic progression, adjusting for age, mechanism of injury, Injury Severity Score, Glasgow Coma Scale on arrival, trauma-bay intubation, and preinjury antithrombotic exposure. Results Of the 817 patients with ICH on initial head CT and documented repeat CT, 401 (49.1%) had radiographic progression. Patients with progression were younger (58 vs. 62 y, p=0.027), more frequently male (71.3% vs. 63.7%, p=0.020), and had similar antithrombotic exposure (15.2% vs. 14.2%, p=0.678). Craniotomy/craniectomy was more frequent among those with progression (21.2% vs. 8.2%, p<0.001). On multivariable analysis, MCH demonstrated the strongest associated risk for progression (odds ratio [OR] 5.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.36-9.33, p<0.001), whereas IPH (OR 2.02, CI: 0.86-4.75, p=0.108), SDH, EDH, and IVH were not independently associated with radiographic ICH progression. Conclusions MCH was independently associated with radiographic ICH progression. This higher-risk hemorrhage pattern may warrant closer neurological monitoring. Level of evidence Prognostic/Epidemiologic; Level III.

title: Anatomical-Persistent Synergy Mamba for Joint Pre-to-Postoperative CT Synthesis and Multi-structure Segmentation in Orbital Decompression Surgery.
abstract: Thyroid Eye Disease (TED) often causes proptosis and optic nerve compression, and orbital decompression surgery is commonly performed to relieve these symptoms. However, postoperative anatomical changes are highly nonlinear and patient-specific due to bone removal and orbital content displacement, which makes reliable preoperative prediction both critical and challenging. Existing methods for pre- to postoperative medical image generation often overlook an important clinical prior that, although surgery induces local structural changes, the overall anatomy of the same patient remains largely consistent, and neglecting this can lead to anatomically implausible deviations. To address this issue, we propose APS-Mamba (Anatomical-Persistent Synergy Mamba), a conditional multi-task framework that takes preoperative CT and surgical information as input and jointly performs postoperative CT synthesis and multi-structure segmentation. The model introduces an anatomical persistence constraint to preserve structural consistency in non-operated regions while allowing realistic local deformations in surgery-related areas. It also incorporates a generation-segmentation synergistic learning strategy. In this design, morphological image synthesis provides predicted variations for segmentation, and segmentation enforces semantic constraints to improve the structural fidelity of generated images. Experiments on a clinical TED dataset demonstrate that APS-Mamba outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both image synthesis (PSNR 28.60 dB, SSIM 91.72%) and segmentation (mean DSC 86.17%). Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the anatomical constraint and synergistic learning strategy in modeling anatomical changes.

title: Q-LCAN: Anatomy-Constrained Quantum-Agentic Systems for MRI-Derived Structural Surgical Digital Twins in Uterine Adenomyosis.
abstract: Accurate patient-specific structural assessment of adenomyosis is essential for fertility-preserving treatment planning, but pelvic T2-weighted MRI is difficult to parse because the uterus, endometrium, ectopic glands, hemorrhagic foci, and adenomyoma are nested, overlapping, and highly imbalanced. We propose Q-LCAN, an anatomy-constrained Quantum-Agentic System that converts MRI into a structured surgical digital twin. A dense 3D decoder first estimates target-specific probability maps and signed distance fields. Five target agents then exchange visual evidence under predefined anatomical axioms, while quantum-enhanced differentiable action projection (Q-DAP) calibrates restricted expand, shrink, or hold actions before vision-language level-set control. A detached anatomical correction module and an independent audit reduce and report residual violations. On 658 multicenter examinations, Q-LCAN achieved case-level five-target macro-average DSC/ASSD of 0.814/2.23 mm in internal five-fold validation and 0.802/2.33 mm in external testing. Compared with the strongest protocol-aligned baseline, Q-LCAN improved macro DSC by 0.018 and 0.019 and reduced ASSD by 0.29 and 0.31 mm, with gains concentrated in ectopic glands, hemorrhagic foci, adenomyoma burden, lesion-to-endometrium distance, residual lesion ratio, and candidate resection-boundary distance. Q-LCAN provides an auditable quantum-agentic framework for MRI-derived structural twins; its millimeter-scale descriptors are intended as preoperative decision support, not autonomous operative guidance.

title: Latent Interpolation Learning Using Diffusion Models for Cardiac Volume Reconstruction.
abstract: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) imaging is a critical tool for diagnosing and managing cardiovascular disease, yet its utility is often limited by the sparse acquisition of 2D short-axis slices, resulting in incomplete volumetric information. Accurate 3D reconstruction from these sparse slices is essential for comprehensive cardiac assessment, but existing methods face challenges, including reliance on predefined interpolation schemes (e.g., linear or spherical), computational inefficiency, and dependence on additional semantic inputs such as segmentation labels or motion data. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Cardiac Latent Interpolation Diffusion (CaLID) framework that introduces three key innovations. First, we present a data-driven interpolation scheme based on diffusion models, which can capture complex, non-linear relationships between sparse slices and improves reconstruction accuracy. Second, we design a computationally efficient method that operates in the latent space and speeds up generative 3D whole-heart upsampling time by a factor of 24, reducing computational overhead compared to previous methods. Third, with only sparse 2D CMR images as input, our method achieves SOTA performance against baseline methods, eliminating the need for auxiliary input such as morphological guidance, thus simplifying workflows. We further extend our method to 2D+T data, enabling the effective modeling of spatiotemporal dynamics and ensuring temporal coherence. Extensive volumetric evaluations and downstream segmentation tasks demonstrate that CaLID achieves superior reconstruction quality and efficiency. By addressing the fundamental limitations of existing approaches, our framework advances the state of the art for spatio and spatiotemporal whole-heart reconstruction, offering a robust and clinically practical solution for cardiovascular imaging. The code is available at https://github.com/niklasbubeck/calid.

title: Can Simple MRI Characteristics Predict Molecular Subgroups in Paediatric Medulloblastoma?
abstract: Introduction Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant paediatric central nervous system (CNS) tumour and is classified using molecular subgroups: WNT, SHH and non-WNT/non-SHH. Subgroup identification guides prognosis and treatment, but requires molecular testing, which is not universally available. MRI is routine in assessment of CNS tumours, and the MRI characteristics may serve as surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subgrouping. This study aims to use simple MRI surrogate markers identified by Perreault et al., against local medulloblastoma cases and their final molecular outcome. Method Retrospective cohort study of paediatric medulloblastomas at a single tertiary children's hospital between January 2015 and October 2025. MRI studies were reviewed by a paediatric neuroradiologist and a radiology registrar in consensus. Tumours were classified by location (cerebellar hemisphere, cerebellopontine angle/cerebellar peduncle (CP/CPA), or midline/fourth ventricle) and enhancement pattern (minimal/none = < 10%, heterogeneous = 10%-90%, solid = > 90%). Associations between MRI features and molecular subgroup were assessed. Results Twenty-two cases were analysed: SHH 22.7% (5/22), WNT 13.6% (3/22) and non-WNT/non-SHH 63.7% (14/22). Most tumours were midline (90.9%), with two hemispheric lesions and no CP/CPA. Enhancement patterns were heterogeneous (54.5%), solid (36.4%) and minimal/none (9.1%). Hemispheric location was associated with SHH tumours (p = 0.043), and all WNT tumours demonstrated solid enhancement (p = 0.036). No other statistically significant associations were identified. Conclusion MRI characteristics offer promising surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subtype. The only strong predictor we found corresponding with Perreault et al. is that hemispheric lesions are correlated with SHH-activated medulloblastoma. This supports further investigation of MRI markers as non-invasive and preoperative medulloblastoma subgroup prediction.

Introduction

Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant paediatric central nervous system (CNS) tumour and is classified using molecular subgroups: WNT, SHH and non-WNT/non-SHH. Subgroup identification guides prognosis and treatment, but requires molecular testing, which is not universally available. MRI is routine in assessment of CNS tumours, and the MRI characteristics may serve as surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subgrouping. This study aims to use simple MRI surrogate markers identified by Perreault et al., against local medulloblastoma cases and their final molecular outcome.

Method

Retrospective cohort study of paediatric medulloblastomas at a single tertiary children's hospital between January 2015 and October 2025. MRI studies were reviewed by a paediatric neuroradiologist and a radiology registrar in consensus. Tumours were classified by location (cerebellar hemisphere, cerebellopontine angle/cerebellar peduncle (CP/CPA), or midline/fourth ventricle) and enhancement pattern (minimal/none = < 10%, heterogeneous = 10%-90%, solid = > 90%). Associations between MRI features and molecular subgroup were assessed.

Results

Twenty-two cases were analysed: SHH 22.7% (5/22), WNT 13.6% (3/22) and non-WNT/non-SHH 63.7% (14/22). Most tumours were midline (90.9%), with two hemispheric lesions and no CP/CPA. Enhancement patterns were heterogeneous (54.5%), solid (36.4%) and minimal/none (9.1%). Hemispheric location was associated with SHH tumours (p = 0.043), and all WNT tumours demonstrated solid enhancement (p = 0.036). No other statistically significant associations were identified.

Conclusion

MRI characteristics offer promising surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subtype. The only strong predictor we found corresponding with Perreault et al. is that hemispheric lesions are correlated with SHH-activated medulloblastoma. This supports further investigation of MRI markers as non-invasive and preoperative medulloblastoma subgroup prediction.

title: Radiographic measurements of cardiac silhouette and skeletal landmarks in companion galahs (Eolophus roseicapilla) and sulphur-crested cockatoos (Cacatua galerita).
abstract: Introduction Cardiac disease is common in companion birds, yet its diagnosis remains a challenge due to limited validated tests. Radiography is frequently used to assess cardiac size in birds; however, interspecies variation necessitates species-specific reference intervals. This study aimed to establish the cardiac silhouette in companion galahs (Eolophus roseicapilla) and sulphur-crested cockatoos (Cacatua galerita). Methods Ventrodorsal (VD) and laterolateral (LL) radiographs of 30 adult galahs and 21 adult cockatoos were obtained from medical records that were admitted to the University of Queensland Veterinary Teaching Hospital from 2013 to 2023. In the VD view, cardiac width (CW) was measured with other anatomical landmarks including thoracic width (TW), clavicular distance (ClD), coracoid width (CoW) and 3rd-4th rib distance (RD). In the LL view, the cardiac length (CL) was measured and correlated to sternal length (SL). Results Significant positive correlations were found between CW and weight ( ρ=0.777 , p < 0.001); CW and TW ( ρ=0.789 , p < 0.001), in galahs. In cockatoos, significant positive correlations were found between CW and CoW ( ρ=0.541 , p = 0.011); CW and ClD ( ρ=0.491 , p < 0.021). The 25th-75th percentile range (PR) for CW:TW ranged from 52 to 62.5% and 60-65% in cockatoos and galahs, respectively. Conclusion In galahs, CW correlated positively with the TW, and the 25th-75th PR for CW:TW should be 60%-65%. In cockatoos, the CW is better correlated to the CoW and ClD with the 25th-75th PRI of 549.5%-609.5% and 91.5%-103.0% respectively. The cardiac silhouette was larger in galahs than in cockatoos.

title: Impact of AI-Assisted Endoscopy on Secondary Review and Referral Decisions in Gastric Cancer Screening: A Multicenter Real-World Study.
abstract: Objectives Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted endoscopy may support gastric cancer screening, but its impact on structured secondary human review remains unclear. We evaluated secondary review modifications and referral decisions before and after AI implementation. Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 5013 screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy examinations performed before (n = 2021) and after (n = 2992) AI implementation. The primary outcome was secondary review modifications. Secondary outcomes included referral for further diagnostic evaluation. Multivariable logistic regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, Helicobacter pylori eradication status, prior-year endoscopy, and endoscopist experience were performed. Interaction analyses according to endoscopist experience and inverse probability of treatment weighting analyses were conducted. No external reference standard was available to verify secondary-review modifications or referral decisions. Results Secondary review modifications increased from 1.2% in the pre-AI period to 3.7% in the AI period (p < 0.01). A significant interaction was observed between AI implementation and endoscopist experience (p for interaction < 0.01), with increased modifications primarily among nonexpert endoscopists. Cancer-related modifications remained uncommon but increased after AI implementation (0.6% vs. 0.2%, p = 0.04). Referral rates decreased from 4.9% to 2.8% (p < 0.01), and AI implementation was independently associated with lower odds of referral (adjusted OR = 0.53; 95% confidence interval = 0.36-0.77). Conclusions AI-assisted endoscopy was associated with lower referral rates; however, secondary review modifications persisted after AI implementation, particularly among nonexpert endoscopists. These findings describe workflow changes and do not establish the clinical validity of the modifications or the appropriateness of referral decisions.

title: Multi-Level Automated Classification of Temporomandibular Joint Degenerative Joint Disease on CBCT Using 3D Volumetric and 2D Slice-Based Approaches.
abstract: Background Temporomandibular joint degenerative joint disease (TMJ DJD) causes progressive osseous changes of the mandibular condyle and articular fossa. Although cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) enables detailed assessment, manual interpretation is time-consuming and subject to inter-observer variability. Objectives To develop and validate a multilevel AI framework for CBCT-based TMJ DJD assessment using three-dimensional classification, quantitative volumetric analysis, and two-dimensional slice-based detection. Methods Full-field-of-view CBCT scans from 222 patients were used for three-dimensional analysis. A 3D V-Net classified condyles into Normal, Osteophyte, Erosion, Flattening, and Severe Degeneration categories. Condylar volume was quantitatively compared between TMJ DJD and non-TMJ DJD groups and among degenerative subgroups. For slice-based analysis, 727 temporomandibular joints from 416 patients were retrospectively evaluated. Automated sagittal slice extraction based on the condylion landmark generated 5787 condylar and 666 articular fossa slices. YOLOv10 was used for multi-lesion detection of six condylar and three fossa categories. Results The 3D V-Net achieved an overall sensitivity of 79.47%. Condylar volume differed significantly between TMJ DJD and non-TMJ DJD groups (ANOVA, p = 0.025), whereas differences among the TMJ DJD subgroups were not statistically significant. For condylar slice-based detection, YOLOv10 achieved 94.0% sensitivity, 82.8% precision, 88.0% F1-score, and 91.3% AP@0.50. For articular fossa detection, YOLOv10 achieved 92.41% sensitivity, 83.91% precision, 87.95% F1-score, and 82.01% AP@0.50. Conclusions Three-dimensional AI enabled overall TMJ DJD classification but showed limited discrimination of specific subgroups, particularly erosion. Volumetric analysis differentiated DJD from non-DJD cases but not among DJD subgroups. In contrast, slice-based YOLOv10 effectively detected and labelled specific condylar and fossa degenerative changes, providing more detailed lesion-level characterization.

title: Polarization Sensitive Optical Coherence Tomography for Surgical Margin Assessment for Canine Soft Tissue Sarcoma.
abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) and skeletal muscle both appear high scattering on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) imaging, which resulted in instances of misclassification by observers in prior soft tissue sarcoma margin assessment studies. Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) is an extension of OCT that provides additional information about tissue polarization contrast. In this prospective study we wanted to evaluate whether PS-OCT improves tissue differentiation and diagnostic accuracy compared to spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) alone. PS-OCT images from surgical margins of 10 resected STS were compared with histopathology to identify characteristic features of normal and neoplastic tissues. Then, six observers of varying OCT image interpretation experience assessed surgical margins from 30 resected STS using SD-OCT alone and SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT. PS-OCT images demonstrated distinct birefringence (optical patterns), corresponding to tissue organization: skeletal muscle exhibited alternating high and low birefringence bands, fascia showed variable birefringence and STS had uniformly low birefringence. Overall diagnostic accuracy was high for both modalities [correct classification rate: SD-OCT alone 93.7% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.1, 96.0) vs. SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT 92.6% (95% = CI: 89.3, 95.4)]; adding PS-OCT did not significantly improve accuracy across all observers (p = 0.82), though expert observers benefited significantly (p = 0.0018). Interobserver and intraobserver agreement ranged from substantial to near perfect. These findings suggest PS-OCT can be interpreted reliably after brief training and may enhance accuracy for experienced users. Further research should explore structured training and real-time applications for comprehensive surgical margin evaluation.

title: A New Application of 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT: Imaging of Cats With Mammary Carcinoma.
abstract: Feline mammary carcinoma (FMC) is an aggressive and highly metastatic cancer that shares molecular and clinical characteristics with human triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), making it a relevant comparative model for a disease lacking targeted therapies. This study investigated the feasibility and clinical utility of 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT imaging in cats with naturally occurring mammary carcinoma. Eight cats (seven tumour-bearing, one healthy control) were administered an intravenous dose of 64 CuCl 2 and underwent whole-body PET/CT imaging. Semi-quantitative analysis was performed using standardized uptake values (SUVs), and tumour-to-muscle ratios were calculated to assess lesion conspicuity. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations were measured as a marker of systemic copper metabolism. All primary masses were 64 Cu-avid and conspicuous, with consistently elevated tumour-to-muscle ratios across tumour-bearing cats, allowing clear differentiation between neoplastic and normal tissue. Imaging provided additional staging information by identifying locally invasive and metastatic disease that was not fully evident on physical examination. Physiologic tracer distribution was characterized by high uptake in the liver and gallbladder and low uptake in skeletal muscle, which served as a reliable reference tissue. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations varied widely and did not correlate with tumour uptake. These findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT is a feasible functional imaging modality for FMC, potentially aiding in tumour detection. This was an exploratory study, and not all imaging results could be confirmed by cytology or histopathology. Nonetheless, our findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT should be investigated further as a method for probing copper utilization in FMC.

title: Clinical Presentation, Acute Clinical Response, Drug Tolerability, and Short-Term Outcome of Cats Treated for Acute Congestive Heart Failure With Pimobendan (2017-2022): 71 Cases.
abstract: Objective To describe clinical effects, drug tolerability, and short-term outcomes of cats treated with pimobendan (PB) in conjunction with other therapies for acute congestive heart failure (CHF). Design Retrospective single-center study (2017 to 2022). Setting Academic teaching and referral hospital. Animals Seventy-one cats with acute CHF treated with PB and furosemide. Treatment included dobutamine (DB) in 15 cases. Measurements and main results Physical examination results, laboratory results, and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scoring were assessed in all cats at admission and 24 h later. Respiratory rate and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scores decreased after 24 h of therapy (p < 0.0001 for both values). Anemia and hypochloremia were more common than azotemia, hyponatremia, and hypokalemia on Day 1. Serum chloride and potassium concentrations decreased, and serum creatinine concentration increased after therapy (p < 0.05), but none of these values was associated with prolonged hospitalization or reduced survival. Cats receiving PB exhibited few adverse clinical signs. Seven of 15 cats (47%) that received concurrent DB therapy were suspected of having adverse effects that responded to decreased dosage or discontinuation of the medication. There was no difference in survival to discharge (p = 0.17) or days of hospitalization (p = 0.78) between cats receiving DB therapy and those that did not. Overall survival to discharge was 76%, and 75% of cats discharged alive were discharged in ≤3 days. Conclusions The short-term prognosis for cats treated for acute CHF was good, and PB therapy appeared to be well tolerated. Most cats showed clinical and radiographic improvement in the first 24 h of therapy and were hospitalized for ≤3 days. The addition of DB to therapy in some cats did not alter survival and was associated with adverse clinical signs in 7/15 cats (47%) treated with DB.

Academic teaching and referral hospital.

Animals

Seventy-one cats with acute CHF treated with PB and furosemide. Treatment included dobutamine (DB) in 15 cases.

Measurements and main results

Physical examination results, laboratory results, and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scoring were assessed in all cats at admission and 24 h later. Respiratory rate and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scores decreased after 24 h of therapy (p < 0.0001 for both values). Anemia and hypochloremia were more common than azotemia, hyponatremia, and hypokalemia on Day 1. Serum chloride and potassium concentrations decreased, and serum creatinine concentration increased after therapy (p < 0.05), but none of these values was associated with prolonged hospitalization or reduced survival. Cats receiving PB exhibited few adverse clinical signs. Seven of 15 cats (47%) that received concurrent DB therapy were suspected of having adverse effects that responded to decreased dosage or discontinuation of the medication. There was no difference in survival to discharge (p = 0.17) or days of hospitalization (p = 0.78) between cats receiving DB therapy and those that did not. Overall survival to discharge was 76%, and 75% of cats discharged alive were discharged in ≤3 days.

Conclusions

The short-term prognosis for cats treated for acute CHF was good, and PB therapy appeared to be well tolerated. Most cats showed clinical and radiographic improvement in the first 24 h of therapy and were hospitalized for ≤3 days. The addition of DB to therapy in some cats did not alter survival and was associated with adverse clinical signs in 7/15 cats (47%) treated with DB.

title: Generalized Megaesophagus Concurrent With Toxocariasis in a Cat.
abstract: Feline megaesophagus is a rare disorder characterized by esophageal hypomotility and dilation, resulting in regurgitation, weight loss, and occasionally death. This report describes the clinical and paraclinical findings of generalized megaesophagus with a possible contribution of toxocariasis in a kitten. A 2-month-old female cat was referred with chief complaints of lethargy, hyporexia, dyspnea, and vomiting/regurgitation. Physical examination of the kitten revealed bradycardia, bradypnea, hypothermia, dehydration, and lung crackles. The most notable laboratory results were leukopenia with severe toxic changes in neutrophils. Radiographic findings were compatible with the diagnosis of generalized megaesophagus. Despite supportive measures, the kitten died the next day. Necropsy revealed diffuse esophageal dilation and Toxocara spp. roundworms in the stomach and duodenum. Histopathology showed an ascarid larva in the esophagus, necrosis and metaplasia in the pylorus, and absence of villi and Brunner's glands in the duodenum. Based on the morphological identification of the adult gastrointestinal nematodes, the final diagnosis was generalized megaesophagus of unspecified classification concurrent with toxocariasis. However, the exact cause of death could not be established. Although respiratory abnormalities raised suspicion of a pulmonary complication, pneumonia was not confirmed. We hypothesized that toxocariasis may have contributed to esophageal dysfunction in this kitten through potential mechanisms such as vomiting, gastrointestinal obstruction, or neurological involvement; however, these mechanisms could not be directly demonstrated. Therefore, parasitic diseases, including toxocariasis, may be considered among potential differential diagnoses or contributing conditions in young cats presenting with megaesophagus, particularly when concurrent gastrointestinal parasitism or related complications are identified. Further studies are required to clarify the possible relationship between toxocariasis and esophageal dysfunction.
